summary.intent: Implement git boundary slice B (trail #494) in the callisto repo: a typed Rev for git revisions, a unified GitPath for literal paths, and move direct `git add` calls into GitAccess, with real-git tests, self-audit, full gate, convergence record and a signed local commit.
summary.outcome: Rev and GitPath were implemented and all callers migrated across callisto-model, graph and cli, with real-git tests added. The full gate was iterated and a signed commit was made; the transcript ends at the commit, so the convergence record, final gate result and sha report are not confirmed.

repo: Git boundary lives in crates/callisto-model/src/vcs (boundary.rs, access.rs, checkpoint.rs, mod.rs); callers in callisto-graph and callisto-cli must go through GitAccess.
The e2e harness has a git allow-list of command shapes that had to be updated to accept `--end-of-options`.
provider_flag_contract_tests.rs probes harness flags against real git and needed updating for `--end-of-options`.
Gate for model signature changes: just pre-push, lint, doc-check, test, plus just fuzz-check because the fuzz crate is outside the workspace.
Graph errors from git failures map through GraphError::Command/Vcs and exit_kind; tests asserting old rev-parse args or error variants needed updating.

code.finding: Plain `git rev-parse --end-of-options <spec>` echoes the flag back as an output line, so blob_hash_at returned the wrong line; `--verify` is needed alongside it.
Rev is constructed only from CommitSha, HEAD, or fully qualified refs/tags/ or refs/heads/ names; GitPath merges Pathspec::literal and check_ignore_arg with per-command spelling inside.

workflow: Probing git behaviour with a scratch script is risky: when its scratch dir couldn't be created it ran in the real worktree and made commits and a tag, which had to be reset and deleted. Always verify the working directory before running such scripts.
Run cargo-mutants only on new decision logic; it surfaced a gap in commit_time that was fixed with a test, and mutants.out was removed before committing.
Run the full gate as a background script and judge each step by exit code; reruns exposed real bugs (rev-parse echo) that scoped tests missed.

friction: Probe script mishap created accidental commits and a tag in the worktree, requiring cleanup.
The gate takes long and had to be rerun several times because of formatting drift, harness allow-list failures, the rev-parse bug and contract tests.
One graph test (npm network) fails in the sandbox and needs unsandboxed runs.
